The one link that was not merely unproven but UNIMPLEMENTED when this row was written — the 'focused-composer comment' — now ships: a pure resolveComposerTarget reducer plus a ComposerFocusStore bind the composer to a FOCUSED review card, the card registers only when the server resolve says this reader may comment, and a bound message travels the CARD's own decision path rather than the model's. HOW THE CHAIN IS PROVEN, stated exactly rather than rounded up: the human-facing links are photographed LIVE on the labeled DEV runtime (https://github.com/cinatra-ai/cinatra/blob/ec30b7513c6541ec01af7dbef1d0a1979dc074f0/evidence/2573-s7-visuals-lane) — A1/A2 the typed chip-row hold and its confirm on the run card, B1–B5 the binding row, the routed comment and the release, C1/C2 the chat-hosted review card pending → decided; every routing claim in that round is checked against cinatra.artifact_review_audit, the app's own audit trail. The machine links — changes_requested closing the base gate and holding the effect, the pinned repair successor, the minted verification record, the release on approve — are proven by the integration suites named above. WHAT IT IS NOT: one continuous scripted Playwright journey on a production build. That shape is unreachable here, not unattempted — the scripted-provider fence and the lifecycle-seed fence make a production-equivalent build and an LLM-backed dispatch mutually exclusive by construction (the fences are quoted in this manifest's AC-15 note), which is the situation entry 334 answer 3 rules on. rows.note: PART MET. The retirement half of this criterion is finished and proven, and nothing recorded below is withdrawn: the fourth renderer really is gone and the gate reads the whole tree for its return. What is corrected is the completeness half. MET — the fourth renderer is gone, and the gate now proves it rather than exempting it. When this row was written the run-detail screen (packages/agents/src/instance-screens.tsx) still drew the recommendation interaction ITSELF: its own park read, its own candidate prefetch and a direct `<RunRecommendationChipRow holdRef={…}>`, bypassing RecommendationHoldCard, the LifecycleCardSurfaceProvider host declaration and the card's authoritative-refetch contract. It was not cosmetic: AgenticRunPanel renders only for `run.status !== 'pending_input'` and a HELD run IS `pending_input`, so on the run-detail page the HELD state was drawn ONLY by the parallel path. The file was allowlisted BY NAME in the one-card gate with that justification, so the gate reported the truth instead of a red nobody could fix in an acceptance lane. cinatra#2710 (defect D-1, `7123d2bf1`) deleted the parallel path: the screen mounts RecommendationHoldCard inside its own `<LifecycleCardSurfaceProvider host="run_card">`, branch-selected by the exported runDetailPanelKind / screenHostsRecommendationCard so exactly one renderer draws on EVERY branch, and the pre-existing double-draw of the decided summary on the agentic branch is gone with it. THIS commit deletes the allowlist entry, which is what makes the gate's pass mean the criterion: it now reads the whole tree and finds no fourth renderer at all. Photographed live: the held run drawn through the card (A1) and the decided summary exactly once (A2). REPOINTED, not withdrawn (cinatra#3047): two proofs above named a branch gate that has since been deleted with the second owner it selected between — the run panel's own copy of the row, which gave one row two placements on the run page. The claim they carried is unchanged and is now proven where it lives: the screen mounts the card on EVERY branch, the panel mounts none, and the row's single root is counted in real DOM on all four branches of runDetailPanelKind. REPOINTED AGAIN, not withdrawn (cinatra#3047, the review's point D): the proof named above measured the settled row's ONE root inside the run detail column. The reviewer's point D moved where that root may stand — "every HITL shows on its own dedicated page; do not show skills on top of a HITL card, the review card, the schedule card or any other card" — so the run detail draws the selected step and nothing above it, and the skills row is the Skills step's own page. The claim this row carries is unchanged and is stronger: the same suite, on all four branches of runDetailPanelKind, now counts ZERO roots in the run detail at the later moments and exactly ONE on the step's own page, and the run-progress panel still draws none. The renamed arm is the one cited; the arms for the held reading, the never-held reading and the rail entry are unchanged in that file.
rows.gap: The criterion has two clauses and they are not in the same state. The named parallel renderers ARE gone and the whole tree is grep-gated for their return, so that clause is met and its proofs stand. 'EXACTLY ONE implementation per interaction' is not met: two of the four interaction kinds have NO implementation of their own and are dispatched to the S1 shell, which draws a line of text and calls itself not-yet-drawn. The gate that reported this row green counted one component serving two kinds as one-per-interaction, so it could only ever see duplicates, never absences. It now checks both directions and its done-check names the two undrawn kinds; this row is honest about the half that is open until they are drawn. The gate's ORDINARY run is now the done-check: the lenient read needs a flag, so "this gate fails while a kind is a placeholder" is true of the run anybody actually makes.

rows.priorNote: SATISFIED under owner ruling entry 334 answer 3 — and the FENCE FINDING that made the ruling necessary is kept here, because it is the reason the criterion could not be met as written. THE FENCE: `assertScriptedProviderNotProduction` (packages/llm/src/scripted-test-provider.ts) throws unless CINATRA_RUNTIME_MODE === 'development' AND NODE_ENV !== 'production'; `lifecycleSeedEnvVerdict` FENCE 1a (src/lib/test-support/lifecycle-seed-fence.ts) answers 404 production-build on NODE_ENV === 'production' before it reads any other gate. `next start` sets NODE_ENV=production and Next inlines that value into the server bundle at build time, so a production-equivalent build and an LLM-backed dispatch are MUTUALLY EXCLUSIVE by construction. Both fences are shipped product safety, not test scaffolding, and this lane weakened neither. WHAT IS PROVEN. Structural conformance, bidirectionally, against the pinned S0 spec commit (design@6c20871b4108176c1d0193f19ecd2947f6c6355f specs/app-lifecycle-cards.html): every spec anchor is rendered, and every anchor the route renders is in the spec's closed set. PRODUCTION-BUILD cells, on a real `pnpm build` + `next start` (https://github.com/cinatra-ai/cinatra/blob/ec30b7513c6541ec01af7dbef1d0a1979dc074f0/evidence/2573-s7-conformance): the review card PENDING on the page gate region with its island iframe, sandbox tokens and server-minted ref; the island rendering the BUILD-MAP renderer class server-side; and the island's ONE empty document for a ref that does not decode. DEV-RUNTIME cells, each labeled (https://github.com/cinatra-ai/cinatra/blob/ec30b7513c6541ec01af7dbef1d0a1979dc074f0/evidence/2573-s7-visuals-lane): the review card on the chat_thread surface PENDING (C1) and DECIDED (C2), and the recommendation hold on the run_card surface HELD (A1) and decided exactly once (A2). Every row photographed there was written by the shipped writers and read back from cinatra.artifact_review_audit; the only stand-in anywhere is the model layer, and the one DB-level fixture (a single agent_assigned_skills row, in the shape the shipped store writes) is stated on the cell. THE ONE OPEN CELL, recorded rather than rounded up: `C3__review-card__run_card__live-run` is NOT delivered. The run_card host IS declared and a real review gate IS bound to the run — its own step rail draws 'Review changes_requested' and 'Core analysis drifted' — but AgenticRunPanel gates the run_card ReviewGateCard on `isPendingApproval && effectiveHitlContext?.xRenderer === ARTIFACT_REVIEW_REDIRECT_RENDERER_ID && reviewGateCardRef`, and that interrupt context is LIVE ORCHESTRATION STATE rather than a row: it needs a run that actually pauses at the artifact-review checkpoint, i.e. a real LLM-backed execution, and no model credential may reach the capture host. The card suite proves the same component draws on that host ('draws the SAME card on every first-party host, differing only in the frame'); what is missing is the photograph of it under a live pause.

specCommitDrift.why: cinatra#3175. The pin above moved to the revision the drawings' main line stands at on 2026-09-01, adopting the three ratifications it had not adopted (design#136, design#138 and design#141). It could not move earlier for a mechanical reason rather than an editorial one: the resolution check refused two of the selector forms the anchor contract records — a class selector and a compound attribute predicate — so the adoption transaction rolled back before it could record what resolves at the new revision, and that refusal is repaired in the same pull request. The pin is an IMMUTABLE commit, never a moving head: a pin that follows the head proves nothing, because the document can change under a green claim.
specCommitDrift.differs: Against the previous pin, measured on the drawing's own text: §V retires the per-skill chip controls — `one chip per skill · confirm / adjust / skip on each` becomes `one pill per skill · a checkbox in front of each name and vendor · one Continue beneath the list`, with the drawing stating that a pill carries nothing to press; §II's decision floor reads `Comment · Regenerate · Continue` where it read `Comment · Reject · Approve`, over one note field rather than the optional rationale field; and a new §XIII draws the fleet's displays on the review card — one review per artifact, the card's states drawn once, only the rendering differing from artifact to artifact. §IX's four-host presence matrix is UNCHANGED row for row, and its only edit is the sentence naming each kind's live affordances, which follows §V. The rows below are unaffected in disposition: nothing here weakens a criterion or closes a MISSING one.
specCommitDrift.whoRatified: STATED EXACTLY, because a pin is a claim about what a drawing says and not about who blessed it. The commit named above is the head of the drawings' main line on 2026-09-01: it has exactly one parent, design@37c39e7f60e548c8eeb14eb4626b8a308eb8f570, and it carries a maintainer-tier Reviewed-by trailer of its own (@groganz), as does each of the three ratifications this move adopts. It does NOT itself touch the drawing this pin governs, and that is stated rather than glossed: the governed drawing's content at this commit is the content design#141 ratified on 2026-08-30 — the same blob id at both commits, 173c691451838319fb64ffdb5a79868ffbc257d7 — and the two earlier ratifications this move adopts are reachable from it.
